newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government wins 23rd confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italian government wins 23rd confidence vote.

text.p: The Italian government won its 23rd lower house confidence vote when it gained approval on Wednesday for a decree aimed at speeding up the process for starting or resuming state construction projects.

The year-old centre-left coalition led by Prime Minister Romano Prodi won by 310 votes to 244. It called the confidence vote to sweep away some 400 ammendments put forward by the separatist Northern League.
The decree, approved by the cabinet nearly two months ago, aims to streamline the approval process for starting or resuming public works projects that have been frozen or stalled.
Decrees lapse unless they are passed by parliament within 60 days and the construction decree had to be approved by May 25.
Prodi's government, which relies on the hard left Communist Refoundation party for a parliamentary majority, has often had to resort to confidence votes to ram measures through the lower house.
Politicians from the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance said the latest confidence vote was undemocratic as it silenced parliamentary debate.
The government in turn accused the opposition of obstructionism in holding up parliamentary business.

The Northern League, which last year proclaimed the symbolic independence of northern Italy, has taken to blocking most government measures with a barrage of ammendments to demonstrate its opposition to the Rome government.
House speaker Luciano Violante described the cycle of blocking tactics followed by confidence votes as "a deathly mechanism" and said it was obstructing parliamentary activity.
The upper house has already approved the construction decree, which is aimed at projects throughout Italy which were frozen as corruption scandals swept away Italy's old political order in 1992.
Some of the projects were exposed as lucrative sources of kickbacks and bribes from contractors.
